facts.fact: OneHealthEHR Inc. says its electronic health record and disease-surveillance platform went into live clinical use in Liberia and Ghana on 1 September 2026, at four facilities growing to seven clinics and health centres in about three weeks across the two countries; the Ghana share is not given.

The company reports seven active clinics and health centres across Liberia and Ghana together by late September 2026, with 30 to 40 clinics and hospitals targeted by December 2026; no Ghana count or denominator is given and the article calls the rollout a pilot.

The company says the platform is offline-first, with clinicians recording patient information during care and synchronising when a connection returns, giving patient information at the point of care (stated for both countries, September 2026).

The platform is run by the private company OneHealthEHR Inc. with a consortium of European technology and research partners; no Ghanaian ministry or public body is named as owner or partner (September 2026).

systems.tiers: clinics and health centres; seven facilities across Liberia and Ghana, Ghana facilities not named
